correctness.rationale: Two exhaustive independent face enumerators agree on 6,497 faces and prove coverage by the seven-edge maximum. Two complete, individually Hasse-acyclic Morse pairings each produce 3,193 pairs and integral signed Morse chain groups with ranks 8,51,40,12 in degrees 3–6. Every integer cancellation has a unit pivot, both residual complexes satisfy differential squared zero, and elementary unimodular reductions leave unit ranks 2 and 4 only. Therefore reduced integral homology ranks are 6,45,36,12 and no torsion at any prime. Separate unreduced mod-two and mod-three boundary ranks and a Hamiltonian cycle count independently match. All computation is reproduced by embedded complete Python source and output; no generalization or homotopy-type assertion is inferred.

originality.rationale: The fixed-object integer result is not implied by the scoped primary results inspected. The 2022 foundational paper analyzes paths, polygons, oriented strips and transitive tournaments. The 2024 general quiver-minor result bounds torsion for bounded genus but does not calculate this cube and its matching-complex identification requires no oriented cycles. The 2026 bidirectional-polygon classification is for degree-two graphs. The 2007 cycle-free chessboard results concentrate on complete digraphs and abstract connectivity, not these lower homology groups. A previously available general top-Hamiltonian-cycle observation covers the degree-six rank and is not treated as new; the contributions are the exact lower degree groups and integral torsion-free conclusion for the whole fixed example. Research-record comparisons use graph-specific aliases and equivalent definitions; no inspected statement dominates those claims. An equivalent unindexed result remains a residual bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: An exact equivalent cube computation may exist in unindexed work or an overlooked appendix.
Top-dimensional rank 12 is already implied by general Hamiltonian-cycle descriptions and is not itself new.
The full homotopy type and higher attaching maps are not established by homology.

value.rationale: The full integral homology is a natural invariant for the standard three-dimensional cube given every arc orientation; it is the first genuinely three-dimensional cubical bidirected example beyond literature on paths, polygons and oriented strips. The face complex is nonpure and has four consecutive nonzero homology degrees, including three newly determined lower groups and absence of integral torsion. These concrete ranks provide a nontrivial canonical comparison benchmark for cubical digraph multipath complexes. The group choice and invariant are structurally motivated, not an arbitrary slice or routine normalization.
